From Abraham Accords to the Mecca Pact

In 2020, Trump’s Middle East architecture had Israel near the center. The Abraham Accords were meant to link Israeli technology, intelligence and military power with Gulf money under an American security umbrella. Saudi normalization was supposed to be the crown piece.

Instead, on August 7 it signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Turkey and Pakistan. An attack on one signatory is now defined as an attack on all three. The pact links Saudi cash, Turkey’s NATO-scale military and fast-growing defense industry, and Pakistan’s armed forces and nuclear status. It includes deeper coordination on exercises, intelligence, air defense, drones, electronic warfare and defense production. 


On Sunday, Trump praised the agreement as a “BIG, BOLD, IMPORTANT FIRST STEP,” saying it showed the Middle East “coming together” and becoming able to defend itself “in a more meaningful way.” 

For Washington, this is burden-sharing. Fewer American troops, fewer direct guarantees, and more regional security paid for and operated by regional allies. The United States does not need every partner to love one another. It needs them to buy weapons, carry risk and stop calling for another carrier group whenever missiles start flying.

The new structure was built without Israel. The agreement does not name Israel as an adversary. Turkish officials have described it as defensive and open to other states. Saudi officials deny it is an axis against any country. 

But one day after the signing, Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Asif called Israel “a threat to the entire Muslim world” and urged a “united military front” against it. Turkish officials and analysts have presented the pact as a way to widen Ankara’s regional deterrence, including against Israeli power. 

The Abraham Accords offered Israel a place inside the regional security system. The Mecca Pact offers a different formula: Saudi money, Turkish military infrastructure and Pakistani deterrence. Israel becomes an outside variable, sometimes a potential partner, sometimes a competitor, sometimes the threat used to sell the arrangement.

Trump supports this not despite American interests, but because of them. America does not need the most loyal ally. It needs a region that requires fewer dollars, fewer soldiers and fewer aircraft carriers.

Yesterday, Israel was meant to share that work with Arab states.
Today, the Arab states have been offered Turkey and Pakistan.
Allies are not betrayed. They are replaced when the contractor changes.

🏁⚔️🇷🇺 NATO has developed three main strategies in the event of a Russian attack in the Baltic states, according to Bild.

The publication claims that a journalist was unofficially shown visualizations of the Alliance's plans during a visit to the U.S. Army command in Europe and Africa. 

In the event of missile and drone strikes, as well as a Russian military offensive, NATO plans to initially suppress Russian missile systems using aircraft, missiles, and drones. One potential target could be the Kaliningrad region, where air defense systems and missile complexes are located.

At the same time, an "autonomous zone" is planned to be created along the borders with Russia and Belarus, where only drones and unmanned ground vehicles will operate against advancing Russian forces, without a permanent presence of NATO troops.

The third element involves strikes within Russia itself, targeting military and logistical facilities such as airfields, defense enterprises, bridges, and railways. The deployment of drones and robots into Russia to attack military bases and airfields is also being considered.

The U.S. Army, however, told the publication that specific assumptions about possible operations against Russia are speculative and do not represent an official position.

Addressing a session of Parliament virtually on Tuesday, Ghalibaf addressed several domestic and regional issues, particularly the US non-compliance with the framework text, also known as the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed by President Donald Trump himself.
​
Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the conditions set out in the MoU are implemented, including lifting the blockade, releasing frozen assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending threats and military operations at all fronts, he stressed.
​
While paying tribute to the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ghalibaf noted that forty-eight years of guidance of Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei prepared the Iranian people and the Armed Forces to stand united and steadfast in the face of aggressions launched by the US and the Israeli regime.
​
Stating that the whole world acknowledged the victory of sovereign and independent Iran over the “criminal, terrorist, and corrupt American–Zionist enemy,” the top parliamentarian rebuked the aggressive regimes in Washington and Tel Aviv for their delusion of overthrowing the sacred system of the Islamic Republic.
​
He said the synergy of the Iranian nation, both in diplomatic and military fields, as well as the public enthusiasm in the streets and the guidance of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, became a testament to America’s defeat, resulting in the joy of Iran’s friends worldwide and the anger of the enemies.
​
Ghalibaf also pointed to Trump’s backing down on the Pakistan-brokered MoU with Tehran, saying the US non-compliance with the document was out of desperation, but it was a massive diplomatic defeat for Washington in practice.
​
He said that the Iranian Armed Forces remained in close consultation with the country’s diplomatic apparatus and gave a practical and crushing response to the breach of promise, showing to the enemy that the Iranian nation, with unity, courage, and rationality, will not hesitate to claim its inalienable rights.
